title: Eustáquio's 92nd-Minute Strike Sends Canada Into the World Cup Round of 16 for the First Time
excerpt: A dramatic stoppage-time goal at SoFi Stadium sealed Canada's first-ever knockout win. For the 1.8 million Indians who call Canada home, the celebration is personal.
body:
Stephen Eustáquio thundered a shot past Ronwen Williams in the 92nd minute on Sunday to give Canada a 1-0 win over South Africa in the opening match of the FIFA World Cup's Round of 32 — the first knockout-round victory in Canadian soccer history.

The game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, had been drifting towards extra time for more than 90 minutes of largely Canadian dominance that yielded seven shots on target but no goals. Then a cross into the South African box bounced off a defender's head, landed at Eustáquio's chest, and the Porto midfielder calmly side-footed the ball into the lower corner. Canada erupted.

"We made everybody back home proud," Eustáquio said afterwards. Coach Jesse Marsch, visibly emotional, called the Round of 16 match that now awaits his team "a free hit."

## History, One Heartbeat at a Time

This is uncharted territory for Canada. Before 2022, the men's team had played in only one World Cup — a winless group-stage exit in 1986. The current generation, led by Alphonso Davies, Jonathan David, and a new cohort of European-based professionals, has transformed the programme into a genuine knockout-stage contender.

Canada co-hosted this tournament alongside the United States and Mexico but was forced to play away from home after finishing second in Group B behind Switzerland. Their path to the Round of 32 included wins over Qatar and a loss to Switzerland that cost them home advantage. Playing in Inglewood instead of Vancouver, Canada became the first World Cup co-host nation to play an elimination game on foreign soil.

The significance was not lost on the players. "You get a chance at one of the two best teams in the world," said defender Alistair Johnston. "It's a pinch-me moment."

## The Road Ahead

Canada's reward is a Round of 16 clash against the winner of Monday's Morocco-Netherlands match in Monterrey, scheduled for Houston on July 4. Neither opponent presents an easy path. The Netherlands topped Group F unbeaten, while Morocco has won two of its three group matches and drew the other against Brazil.

Marsch's team will need to fix the finishing that deserted them for 90 minutes against South Africa. Canada held a 1.32-to-0.13 edge in expected goals and created multiple clear opportunities, including a Derek Cornelius header saved by Williams and several shots cleared off the line. The defence, meanwhile, held firm despite South Africa's occasional counterattacking threat.

Alphonso Davies, introduced as a substitute in the 75th minute, instantly troubled the South African defence with his pace on the left flank. His fitness and availability for the Round of 16 will be crucial.


## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

Canada is home to one of the world's largest Indian diaspora communities — over 1.8 million people of Indian origin, the fastest-growing demographic in the country. In cities like Brampton, Surrey, and Mississauga, World Cup fever has transcended any single national team allegiance.

With India absent from the tournament, many NRIs in Canada have thrown their support behind the host nation. Social media has been full of posts from Indian-Canadians celebrating with flags from both countries, and watch parties in Brampton and the Greater Toronto Area have drawn thousands.

Canada's run is not just a co-host's story — it is becoming a shared celebration for a country whose identity, on and off the pitch, is being reshaped by its immigrant communities.

**Sources:** Fox Sports, CNN, USA Today, Khel Now
